title: Data structures
literature: CLRS; Sedgewick; Okasaki Purely Functional Data Structures; Knuth TAOCP; database index structures (B-tree/LSM) DDIA.

members.name: B-tree
members.what: Self-balancing wide-fanout search tree whose nodes hold many keys sized to a block/page, keeping the tree shallow; B+ trees keep all values in linked leaves for range scans.

members.name: Binary Heap (Priority Queue)
members.what: Implicit complete binary tree stored in an array maintaining the heap order property, giving O(log n) insert and extract-min/max with no pointers.

members.name: Binary Search Tree
members.what: Binary tree maintaining the search-order invariant (left < node < right); self-balancing variants (red-black, AVL) guarantee O(log n) ordered operations.

members.name: Bitmap / Bitset
members.what: Dense array of bits representing set membership or boolean flags by index, supporting bulk bitwise set operations word-at-a-time; compressed variants (Roaring, WAH) handle sparse ranges.

members.name: Bitmap Index
members.what: An index that keeps, for each distinct value (or value range) of a column, a bitmap with one bit per row; multi-predicate queries are answered by bitwise AND/OR/NOT over the bitmaps before touching any rows.

members.name: Bloom Filter
members.what: Bit array plus k hash functions answering approximate set membership with no false negatives and a tunable false-positive rate.

members.name: Bounding Volume Hierarchy
members.what: Tree whose nodes are bounding volumes (typically AABBs) enclosing their children, with scene objects at the leaves, letting intersection queries prune whole subtrees.

members.name: Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT)
aka: G-Counter / PN-Counter / G-Set / OR-Set / LWW-Register / RGA (family members, folded)
members.what: Family of replicated data types (counters, sets, registers, sequences) whose merge operations are commutative/associative/idempotent, so concurrently edited replicas converge without coordination.

members.name: Consistent Hashing
members.what: Hashing scheme placing keys and buckets on the same ring so each key maps to the nearest bucket, remapping only ~1/n of keys when a bucket joins or leaves; virtual nodes smooth the load.

members.name: Copy-on-Write B-Tree
members.what: A B-tree whose updates never modify pages in place: changed pages and their ancestors up to the root are rewritten to new locations, and commit is an atomic root swap.

members.name: Count-Min Sketch
members.what: Sub-linear 2-D counter array indexed by multiple hash functions that answers approximate frequency queries over a stream, with one-sided (over-count) error.

members.name: Deque
members.what: Sequence container supporting O(1) insertion and removal at both ends, typically as a ring buffer or blocked array.

members.name: Disjoint-Set (Union-Find)
members.what: Forest of trees tracking a partition of elements into disjoint sets, with union-by-rank and path compression making find/union near-constant amortized.

members.name: Dynamic Array
members.what: Contiguous array that grows by amortized capacity doubling (and optionally shrinks), preserving O(1) amortized append and O(1) random access.

members.name: Embedded Pointer
members.what: Embed the pointers that maintain a collection directly into each member object instead of allocating external link nodes.

members.name: Erase-Remove
members.what: Combine std::remove/remove_if (which compacts kept elements) with container erase to actually delete matching elements from a sequence container.

members.name: Fenwick Tree
members.what: Implicit array-based tree exploiting binary index decomposition to maintain prefix sums with O(log n) point update and prefix query in n words of memory.

members.name: Fixed-Capacity Container
members.what: STL-style containers whose maximum capacity is a compile-time parameter, storing elements in embedded (static or stack) storage with no heap use.

members.name: Gap Buffer
members.what: Contiguous text buffer with a movable gap of free space at the cursor position, making localized insertions and deletions O(1) until the gap moves or fills.

members.name: Hash Array Mapped Trie (HAMT)
members.what: Trie over hash-code bit chunks using per-node bitmaps to compress sparse children, giving an efficiently persistent (structurally shared, immutable) hash map.

members.name: Hash Table
members.what: Key-value store mapping keys through a hash function into an array of buckets, with collisions resolved by separate chaining or open addressing (linear/quadratic probing, Robin Hood, cuckoo, Swiss-table variants folded here).

members.name: HyperLogLog
members.what: Cardinality-estimation sketch that hashes items and records maximum leading-zero runs in a small register array, estimating distinct counts within a few percent using kilobytes.

members.name: Interval Tree
members.what: Search tree over intervals (typically a BST augmented with subtree max-endpoints) answering which stored intervals overlap a query point or interval in O(log n + k).

members.name: Inverted Index
members.what: Mapping from each term to the sorted list of documents (and positions) containing it, the core structure of full-text search engines.

members.name: k-d Tree
members.what: Binary space-partitioning tree that splits points on alternating coordinate axes, supporting nearest-neighbor and orthogonal range queries in low dimensions.

members.name: Linked List
members.what: Sequence of nodes each holding an element and a pointer to the next (and optionally previous) node, giving O(1) insertion/removal at a known position without element movement.

members.name: Lock-Free FIFO Queue (Michael-Scott)
members.what: A linked-list MPMC queue where enqueue and dequeue advance head/tail with CAS, and threads help complete a lagging tail swing before proceeding.

members.name: Lock-Free Stack (Treiber)
members.what: A linked LIFO where push and pop swing the top-of-stack pointer with a CAS retry loop (with an ABA guard when nodes are recycled).

members.name: LSM Tree
members.what: Write-optimized index that batches writes in an in-memory table, flushes them as sorted immutable runs (SSTables), and merges runs in the background via compaction.

members.name: Merkle Tree
members.what: Tree whose leaves are hashes of data blocks and whose internal nodes hash their children, so one root hash authenticates the whole set and any block is verifiable with a log-length path.

members.name: MinHash
members.what: Similarity sketch storing the minimum hash values of a set under many hash functions, so sketch agreement estimates Jaccard similarity between sets.

members.name: Navigation Mesh
members.what: A data structure representing an environment's walkable space as connected convex polygons, over which agents path-find polygon-to-polygon and then smooth (e.g. string-pulling/funnel) within the free space.

members.name: Persistent Data Structure
members.what: A data structure whose update operations return a new version while old versions remain valid, sharing unchanged substructure between versions.

members.name: Piece Table
members.what: Edit representation keeping the original file and an append-only add buffer immutable, with the document described as a sequence of pieces (spans) into the two buffers.

members.name: Quadtree / Octree
members.what: Hierarchical spatial partition recursively subdividing 2D space into four quadrants (or 3D into eight octants) until cells meet an occupancy or depth bound.

members.name: Queue (FIFO)
members.what: First-in-first-out collection with enqueue at the tail and dequeue at the head, array- or list-backed.

members.name: R-tree
members.what: Balanced B-tree-like index of minimum bounding rectangles that may overlap, grouping nearby spatial objects for disk-friendly window and containment queries.

members.name: Rope
members.what: Balanced binary tree of string fragments representing a long string, making concatenation, insertion, and splitting O(log n) instead of O(n) copies.

members.name: Scene Graph
members.what: Represent a scene as a hierarchy of nodes whose spatial transforms (and other attributes) compose parent-to-child, so moving a parent moves its whole subtree.

members.name: Secondary Index
members.what: An auxiliary structure mapping non-primary-key attribute values to record locations (or primary keys), maintained alongside the base data on every write.

members.name: Segment Tree
members.what: Complete binary tree over an array where each node stores an aggregate (sum, min, max) of its range, giving O(log n) range queries and point/range updates.

members.name: Skip List
members.what: Sorted linked list augmented with probabilistic express lanes at multiple levels, giving expected O(log n) search/insert/delete without rebalancing.

members.name: Slot Map
members.what: Contiguous object pool addressed by stable keys that pair a slot index with a generation counter, so freed-and-reused slots invalidate stale handles while keeping O(1) access and dense iteration.

members.name: Sparse Set
members.what: Pair of arrays (dense packed elements plus sparse index-by-value) representing an integer set with O(1) insert, delete, membership, and clear, and cache-friendly iteration over only the members.

members.name: Spatial Partition
members.what: Store objects in a data structure organized by their spatial position (grid, quadtree, BSP, etc.) so that location-based queries need only examine nearby cells.

members.name: Stack
members.what: Last-in-first-out collection with push/pop/peek at one end, whether array- or list-backed.

members.name: Suffix Array
members.what: Sorted array of all suffix start positions of a text, supporting binary-search substring queries; the array-based, cache-friendly successor to the suffix tree.

members.name: t-digest
members.what: Mergeable sketch of a numeric distribution built from size-varying centroid clusters, estimating quantiles (esp. extreme percentiles) accurately in constant memory.

members.name: Trie
members.what: Tree keyed by successive symbols of the key, so all descendants of a node share a common prefix; radix/Patricia variants compress single-child chains into one edge.

members.name: Uniform Spatial Hash Grid
members.what: Partition of space into uniform cells whose coordinates hash into buckets of contained objects, so neighborhood queries examine only nearby cells.

members.name: Zipper
members.what: A representation of a position inside an immutable structure as the focused element plus its inverted surrounding context, allowing O(1) local edits and navigation.

members.name: Zone Map
members.what: A tiny per-block summary (typically min/max, optionally count/sum) kept for each zone of contiguously stored tuples; scans consult the summaries first and skip every block whose value range cannot satisfy the predicate.
